taxonomy: Seven requested analytical responsibilities, not a verified universal taxonomy

loop.finding: Product-owned Rust run_turn sampling/continuation loop, cancellation and turn state; model responses do not themselves own host execution.

tools.finding: ToolRouter/registry resolves named calls and exposure; tool invocation is separated from model response parsing.

context.finding: AGENTS.md management, retained session context and inline/remote compaction are explicit subsystems; availability depends on configuration/features.

safety.finding: ToolOrchestrator coordinates approval, sandbox selection and retries after denial; network approvals and filesystem authority are host concerns. Presence is not a proof of complete isolation.

orchestration.finding: Agent control has explicit spawn and shared rollout-budget accounting; multi-agent features are supported, not necessary for every task.

extensions.finding: Product-owned plugin catalogue/loader and extension crates; tools include deferred discovery. Protocol integration does not identify a general agent-framework-owned loop.

memory.finding: Session history/compaction and separate memories extension exposing bounded list/search/read/ad-hoc-note operations. Persisted memory and current source truth are distinct.

loop.finding: GeminiClient.sendMessageStream/Turn implements product-owned continuation; MAX_TURNS=100 at inspected snapshot and loop-detection exits. This is not a whole-job cost guarantee.

tools.finding: Tool registry plus Scheduler handles execution states, hooks/confirmation, and batches contiguous tools marked parallelizable.

context.finding: Dedicated chat compression service and hierarchical repository memory loading; compressed history is distinct from original project files.

safety.finding: PolicyEngine makes allow/deny/ask decisions with workspace/trust and command checks; configured modes can change confirmation behavior.

orchestration.finding: LocalAgentExecutor provides typed subagent runs with max-turn termination and cancellation. A2A SDK appears in core dependencies for interoperability.

extensions.finding: Extension loader, MCP SDK/tools and hooks extend product-owned scheduling. GenAI and A2A/MCP SDK dependencies are not evidence of LangGraph-style loop ownership.

memory.finding: Explicit save-memory tool/private project notes, hierarchical GEMINI.md instructions and separately documented auto-memory modes. Feature behavior is version-specific.

loop.finding: Coder.run_one/send_message applies edits and reflects errors with a max_reflections bound. Different edit-format coder classes share product-owned control.

tools.finding: Coding is largely structured text edit extraction/application, with lint/test/shell-command helpers. Do not assume every harness needs native function-call tools.

context.finding: RepoMap selects repository structure with token budgeting; editable/read-only file context and ChatSummary manage history.

safety.finding: Explicit user confirmations for suggested shell commands and file/edit preparation; Git/dry-run support. These are not an OS sandbox guarantee.

orchestration.finding: ArchitectCoder can pass an architect response to a separate editor coder/model after configurable confirmation; sequential role separation, not a mandatory agent swarm.

extensions.finding: Coder subclasses/edit formats and commands are local extension points. Optional /help uses LlamaIndex VectorStoreIndex; it is peripheral retrieval rather than the principal coding loop.

memory.finding: Persisted chat history restoration, bounded conversation summarization and source/Git state; no evidence here that long-term autonomous semantic memory is required.

loop.finding: Current OpenHands/OpenHands is Agent Canvas frontend, not the execution core. Linked software-agent-sdk owns Agent.step and LocalConversation.run, including max_iteration_per_run.

tools.finding: SDK tool registry defines tools; Agent dispatches actions and observations; separate tool package implements terminal/file/browser/delegation capabilities.

context.finding: Append-only event log plus View and condenser events; summarization changes the LLM view while retaining the event record, with soft/hard condensation triggers.

safety.finding: SDK confirmation policies AlwaysConfirm/NeverConfirm/ConfirmRisky are separate from execution isolation. Canvas docs warn local host mode exposes filesystem; Docker mode differs.

orchestration.finding: Agent Server hosts conversations; delegate/child-conversation tools implement additional agents. The SDK is itself reusable agent infrastructure built by OpenHands.

extensions.finding: Typed SDK tools, skills and MCP tools, plus Canvas ACP backend connections. Distinguish own reusable SDK from dependence on third-party general agent frameworks.

memory.finding: Persisted conversation/event state and a two-tier user/project MEMORY.md loader with explicit 6000-character budget; daily logs are loaded on demand.

loop.finding: DefaultAgent.run calls step -> query -> execute_actions over a linear message list; step/cost/wall-time and consecutive-format-error limits are configurable. Zero disables several limits; cost limit is checked before a call and can overshoot.

tools.finding: Environment.execute receives command actions; local environment uses shell subprocesses and completion sentinel, Docker environment changes execution boundary. Bash-only does not mean no host abstractions.

context.finding: DefaultAgent sends current linear message history and rendered task/system templates; no default retrieval graph/compactor is present in this inspected core class.

safety.finding: InteractiveAgent supports confirm/human/yolo; local command timeout kills process group on POSIX. Local execution is not a sandbox. Environment choice and external isolation matter.

orchestration.finding: Model, environment, agent and run scripts are separated; benchmark runners can schedule multiple independent instances. No multi-agent planner is needed by DefaultAgent.

extensions.finding: Small Python classes/config and Model/Environment interfaces; Jinja/Pydantic/LiteLLM supply templates, schema/config and transport, not a third-party agent graph owning the loop.

memory.finding: Trajectory serialization saves messages, config, exit status, model stats; default run resets messages. Saved trajectory is not evidence of a built-in cross-task learning system.

loop.finding: Core implementation unavailable in inspected public repository. README documents an agentic terminal tool; changelog references continuation, max-turns and Stop behavior. Do not infer dependency/control internals from these descriptions.

tools.finding: Public changelog documents Read/Edit/Write/Bash/ToolSearch/MCP behavior and fixes; plugin hook examples expose lifecycle surfaces. Dispatch implementation remains opaque.

context.finding: Changelog documents compaction, context-window state and CLAUDE.md/rules loading. Website architecture docs failed proxy access, so detailed internals are unknown here.

safety.finding: Changelog documents permission modes/rules, host callback or permission-dialog decisions, and safety fixes. Public security-guidance hook is an example, not proof of complete enforcement.

orchestration.finding: Changelog and official plugin docs describe subagents and specialized agent workflows. Scheduling internals and core framework dependencies cannot be audited from public core source.

extensions.finding: Official repository documents plugins bundling commands, agents, skills, hooks and MCP servers. These extension sources are available; core source is not.

memory.finding: Changelog documents nested CLAUDE.md/rules and auto-memory MEMORY.md loading/edits. This establishes documented capability only, not implementation correctness or architectural equivalence with open tools.
